utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Good morning, Ms. Sutherland. Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, we finished yesterday afternoon discussing the police in relation to the Variant A/B document instructions, but I just want to take you back for a moment to paragraph 17 of your report, where you're discussing the -- the discussions that are taking place between Karadzic and his interlocutors in relation to posts within the MUP. And in paragraph 17 you say: "Karadzic also insisted that those Serbs who were appointed holding important positions ..." and you refer to an intercept of the 2nd of September, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could I please have 65 ter number 31885 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This intercept also is discussed in paragraph 18 of your report. Did Zepinic in this intercept discuss with Karadzic the fact that the SDS were occupying more of the commanding posts than they were in fact entitled to?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Objection, leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, but -- let me see. Could you indicate the passage or -- and reformulate the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think there is some latitude in relation to expert witnesses, but if we can go to page 10 of the English and page 12 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What is Dr. Karadzic discussing with Zepinic at that point in the conversation? And first of all, before you answer, did you listen to the audio-tape of this intercept?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have listened to the audio-tape of this intercept, and in fact listened to the audio-tape of all of the intercepts that are cited in my report, not least so that I could compare the audio with the transcribed text to make sure that they were accurate. In this conversation, this is one of very many that I refer to in the report, in which Drs. Zepinic and Karadzic are discussing personnel issues and particularly the number of Serbs, and I would also point out the nature of Serbs or character of Serbs employed by the then-joint Bosnian MUP. Here we have an awareness on this page in front of us that they -- as Zepinic, in fact, says, that we -- that they are occupying more posts than they were entitled to and there's some discussion about this. I would point out in respect of paragraph 17 and indeed it's a point I come back to repeatedly. For example, also in paragraph 22 of my report, that it was very important from the perspective of Dr. Karadzic and the Serbian Democratic Party not only that a sufficient number of Serbs be employed in the police, but they in fact -- that they in fact be Serbs who were loyal to the party line of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Also, Dr. Nielsen, you will find the intercept in appendix B in the binder down beside you. And again the reference is -- I think it's document number 4 in that binder, but it's 65 ter number 31885. If I can just take you to a passage on page 16 in the English and page 13 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I can't find it in the binder here, but I'll look at the screen. Ah, here it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is there a passage on that page that you were just discussing a moment ago? Is -- is Karadzic warning Zepinic that things must be done as the party orders and not as somebody else orders?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is not an isolated case. This is again one of a number of conversations. On the B/C/S, near the top of the page Karadzic is saying: Please bring over all the people here who have been employed in the name of the SDS. We posted them to those positions through our victory in the elections and I have something to say to them. This is again the notion that -- this does not mean that these persons in the police are SDS party members, but it means that from Karadzic's point of view they inhabit or sit on those posts by virtue of the SDS's victory in the elections, and therefore in implementing decisions and in performing their work in the MUP they should adhere to the wishes of the party.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask for that document to be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI P2963, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, we have an incredibly large amount of material to get through today, so I would ask you if you could keep your answers to be as brief as possible. By February 1992 is Mr. Karadzic content with the appointment of personnel within the MUP?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. By February 1992, Karadzic continues to be very distraught with the -- what he perceives to be the discrimination against Serb employees and the interests of the Serbs in the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And I think this is discussed at paragraph 55 of your report. In paragraph 56 you describe a meeting that occurred on the 11th of February, 1992; that is, the minutes of that meeting is an exhibit P01083, so I don't intend calling that up onto the screen. But what was discussed at the 11th of February meeting, and this is appendix A, document number 6, 65 ter number 05413.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I discuss the 11 February 1992 meeting which took place in Banja Luka in paragraphs 56 and the following paragraphs in my report. The key conclusions from this meeting related to a desire to effect the establishment of a separate Serbian Ministry of Internal Affairs in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and it can be said that this idea of such a Serbian ministry had grown out gradually from the previous discussions of decentralising internal affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And having decided that they wanted to form a Serb Ministry of Internal Affairs, did there come a time when the Bosnian Serbs passed a law on this?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. In late February, I believe it was on the 23rd of February, 1992, the Assembly of the Serbian nation in Bosnia and Herzegovina passed a law establishing a Serbian Ministry of Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter number 01002 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is this the law that was passed?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. And I see that the date of its proclamation is rather the 28th of February. I erred in my memory there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I think this is discussed at paragraph 95 of your report.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender that document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, it will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P2964, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: On appendix B, Dr. Nielsen, 65 ter number 18280 is the Republika Srpska MUP rule book on internal organisation, and this is discussed in chapter 3 at paragraphs 175 to 188 of your report. Does the rule book provide an explanation of the internal structure and the function of the RS MUP?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, without bringing that document up onto the screen, I seek to tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: We don't object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is what we see on the monitor?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2965, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In paragraph 80 of your report you cite to a letter dated the 23rd of March, 1992, from Karadzic, re: Steps being taken to staff police around-the-clock. That's Exhibit P02560. I don't intend calling it up on the screen, but do you -- who was this letter sent to?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This letter was sent to the municipal presidents of the SDS in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In paragraph 81 of your report you cite to an RS Assembly session held on the 24th of March, 1992, which is Exhibit P00961. Can you briefly discuss what was discussed at the Assembly meeting and by whom in relation to the police?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At both the 12th and 13th Sessions of the Bosnian Serb Assembly, which were held on the same day, the 24th of March, 1992, and indeed also at the previous session of the Assembly, the 11th Session, there were discussions of the establishment of Bosnian Serb Ministry of Internal Affairs in Bosnia and Herzegovina. And as indicated in paragraph 81, Dr. Karadzic placed great weight on the establishment of such a police force, and he indicated to the Assembly representatives that in the very near future some events would take place in which the police would play a key role. And he then emphasized that the police must be under the control of the civilian authority and must obey it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, you referred to the 13th Session, that's Exhibit P01354.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is there something wrong in emphasizing that police must be under the control of the civilian authority? Or something odd?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think so at all, Your Honour. I regard it as the normal state of affairs with the police in any country, but I think it's very important to highlight that that statement was made at the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why do you find it important?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the context of the subsequent performance of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, this indicates, from my point of view as an analyst, a strong desire to keep the police under civilian control, which is relevant in the light of the fact that there were subsequent protracted discussions in the Republika Srpska about who was really controlling the police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Back to you, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: At the 13th Session held on the 24th of March, was that the session where Mico Stanisic was appointed as minister of the Serbian MUP?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In paragraph 89 of your report, you mention that on the 31st of March, 1992, Momcilo Mandic sent a dispatch, which is Exhibit P01116. What was the essence of the dispatch?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The essence of the dispatch of the 31st of March, 1992, was to announce that on the following day the Bosnian Serb Ministry of Internal Affairs in the Serbian Republic would start to function. I believe that I've previously in my testimony in other cases referred to this as a birth certificate of sorts of the RS MUP.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I want to turn now to discuss the importance of the RS MUP from April 1992. Did Mico Stanisic issue any orders with respect to MUP units and their involvement with the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mico Stanisic in his capacity as minister of RS MUP issued quite a large number of orders and dispatches related to the role of the police vis-a-vis the Army of Republika Srpska. The most important one perhaps is the one dated 15 May 1992, where three days after the establishment of the Army of Republika Srpska, Mico Stanisic attempts to lay out clear lines for the command and control of the police, particularly in circumstances where police forces would be resubordinated to the military.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter number 05292 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is that the document you were just referring to?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And what does he say about any operations to be conducted?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, it's important that this order notes -- and something that's confirmed in other later documents, that the police is regarded as part of the armed forces of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and is to be engaged in what Mico Stanisic refers to, the defence of the territory of that republic. In this order one of the key points is that the police will be organised, and indeed the entire ministry will be organised, into so-called war units which are to be able to participate extensively in combat operations, as indeed subsequent documents show that they do. And they set up a command structure which, among other things, outlines what the framework will be for co-operation with the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And if we can just go to page 2, please, in the English, paragraph 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is that the -- what you were just discussing there, paragraph 7, and then going over onto page 3?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, on the second page of the original of the document we see that a staff, a command staff, is being formed in which the minister for internal affairs is the commander of the command staff. And in paragraph 7 we have a clear statement, that the use of units of the ministry in co-operation with the armed forces of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina can be ordered by the minister for internal affairs. And during periods of resubordination -- or I should say even during periods of resubordination, the minister of internal affairs makes clear that units are to be -- of the police are to be directly commanded through designated employees of the ministry and that the Ministry of Internal Affairs ultimately retains bureaucratic control of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you say something, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes. This will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2966, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, was the RS MUP a constituent part of the RS armed forces formally?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was. And as I point out in the beginning of the section of my report entitled: "RS MUP and the War in Bosnia and Herzegovina," beginning on page 54, the RS MUP played a major role according to its own documents in the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1992. And in the words of Biljana Plavsic and other politicians and indeed in the words of officials of the ministry itself, the RS MUP in the early days of the war acted as an army - I want to make it clear that that's their word - as an army of the RS.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And this is I think referred to in paragraph 191 of your statement -- your report?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. And it is also confirmed by numerous later documents produced by the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So in essence, what was the role played by the RS MUP in the war in BiH?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that perhaps the best way of answering that question is that if we jump to paragraph 380 of my report where I discuss the 1992 RS MUP draft annual report, I quote that report, stating that, and I quote: "Since the very beginning of the war, almost the entire available personnel of the organs for internal affairs have been involved in war activities for the liberation of occupied territories and the protection of liberated Serbian territories. This in good measure also persists today." And quote: "And the RS MUP also in its own words thought that it had made 'a significant contribution' in the struggle of the Serbian nation."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And that draft report is 65 ter number 11241, which we will get to a little bit later on. Can you describe for the Chamber the role that the RS MUP played in the take-overs?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As indicated by some of the documents we saw yesterday and early this morning, from the point of view of the Bosnian Serb leadership, taking control over the police in areas which they wished to see included in a Bosnian Serb entity was crucial. After April 1992 or after the beginning of April 1992, we see a pattern, that while differing from municipality to municipality, overall conforms to a trend in which the police play a crucial role in establishing the authority of the Bosnian Serb Republic. Subsequent documents produced by the police of a analytical nature, for example, their quarterly and annual reports produced in 1992 and later, confirm that the Bosnian Serb police perceived its role to be to assist in implementing the goals of the Serbian Democratic Party in establishing the power of the Bosnian Serbs or the authority of the Bosnian Serbs on the territory that they regarded as their own. I want to indicate also that these actions by Bosnian Serbs in the police predated in many cases April 1992; that is to say, documents produced by the Bosnian Serbs themselves indicate that measures to effect a take-over of authority in parts of Bosnia and Herzegovina significantly in many cases predated the actual establishment of the police in April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, just briefly, in paragraphs 192 to 195 you discuss the issue of the loyalty oaths after the Serbs took power in the municipalities. In that regard, were the public police stations renamed in any way?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it's significant to note that particularly in the first three months of the existence of RS MUP, many of the public security stations, the SJBs, at the municipal level while retaining the name "public security station," added the adjective "Serbian" to the beginning of that phrase, that is, "Serbian public security stations," and that in some cases is reflected in the stamps and seals that they used as well, thereby emphasizing the ethnic nature of the new police force.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And did many non-Serb police officers have an aversion to signing the loyalty oath?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly it appears that police officers of Muslim and Croat ethnicity who were present on territories in which Serbian police stations were being established under the control of RS MUP, in many cases did not desire and objected to swearing any types of solemn statements or oaths to these new police stations. I discuss that, for example, in paragraph 194. And perhaps the best indication of the overall trend of employment of Croats and Muslims in the RS MUP is that by the middle of the summer of 1992 a total of six non-Serbs, that is, six Muslims or Croats, remained in the entire Ministry of Internal Affairs according to the documents of that ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Turning now to -- in relation to combat operations. In paragraph 215 of the report there's reference to the RS MUP forces co-operating with the JNA and the TO; and in paragraph 216, subordination to the VRS. But I think you testified a little earlier that the police units were ultimately responsible to the MUP; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I testified is that during periods when the police are resubordinated to the military of the RS, the Army of the RS, any orders given to those police officers who are resubordinated to those units were, according to Mico Stanisic's 15 May order, supposed to go through the designated police commander of such units. And when I state that the police was ultimately responsible to the MUP, what I meant by that is that at such time that the police would be finished in the operation, a specific combat operation that the minister of internal affairs had authorised, they could not be redeployed to yet further combat activities without the military first coming back to the police, to the minister of internal affairs, and seeking permission to resubordinate them, again, to new operations. This I would note, as reflected in meetings of the MUP leadership in the summer of 1992, was a point of some contention between the police and the army. And I know that they had meetings to resolve disputes about how this was actually going to be implemented in practice.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter number 05682 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, this is in appendix A, document 15. It's a report on the analysis of the work of the SJBs in 1992 on the territory of the CSB Banja Luka. And you cite that in your report at footnotes 192, 242, 250, 380, and 558. In that document they discuss combat operations. What were one of the tasks undertaken by the police during -- in combat operations -- or one of the first tasks I should say?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: During combat operations undertaken in the summer of 1992, the police co-operated with the military in seeking to disarm the population, in particular the Bosnian Muslim and Bosnian Croat population of areas in which the Serbian Republic was asserting its control. I would just note briefly since it links into a point that I mentioned earlier, that page 2 of the B/C/S of -- or actually, with the cover, it's page 3 of the B/C/S document refers to the fact that the police largely accepted the programme of the SDS even though most of the police were not members of that party.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I think that's also on page 3 of the English for Mr. Registrar. In paragraphs --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I would seek to tender that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: My apologies. Yes, that will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2967, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, in paragraphs 203 and 204 you discuss Crisis Staffs charging the relevant SJBs with the implementation of decisions on the disarming of the non-Serbian population and them closely -- or them controlling or closely co-ordinating with the municipal police. Was it the case that in every municipality the chief of the SJB was a member of the Crisis Staffs?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. And as such, the police and the Crisis Staffs co-operated closely throughout the summer of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You mentioned a moment ago about six Muslims being left in the RS MUP. That's actually discussed at paragraph 208, and footnote 250 refers to an exhibit, P02760. I want to turn now to the system of reporting within the RS MUP, and that's dealt with at paragraphs 236 to 243 of your report. You say at paragraph 236 that Stanisic -- Mico Stanisic orders daily bulletins to be sent. And you also make reference to the fact that on the 22nd of April, 1992, at an expanded meeting of the National Security Council, of which Karadzic is in charge of, that the RS government directed the RS MUP to report daily on the situation on the territories of the Republika Srpska. What evidence did you find to show whether there was this reporting going on?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through my research I was able to collect a substantial quantity of these daily bulletins, which to my mind indicated that Mico Stanisic's order was indeed implemented. And one can see in the course of the summer of 1992 that information which is reflected in dispatches sent from the municipal or SJB level to the regional or CSB level is duly collated at the regional level and sent to the Ministry of Internal Affairs and is then in -- once again collated and paraphrased or reproduced in some form in the daily bulletins in the ministry itself. It is indeed the case that there are times at which for, sometimes a number of days, that one police station at a municipal level or several of them or even a whole region for short periods will not be furnishing information because of difficulties with communication, but overall the general pattern is one of regular communication throughout the hierarchy of the RS MUP. And I would note finally that the draft 1992 RS MUP annual report indicates that these daily bulletins, along with much other information, were forwarded to the organs of the RS government, both the government itself and the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And again you make reference to the draft annual report, that -- and I said earlier that that was 65 ter number 11241. That is actually been exhibited now in our case -- in the case, Exhibit P02761.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could quickly call that exhibit number up. If we could go to page 22 to 23 of the English and page 31 to 33 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You referred earlier to the number of bulletins that they received -- that the government were receiving.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In paragraph 389 of my own report, I note that approximately 150 issues of the bulletin of daily events were produced by the RS MUP in the course of the period from April to December 1992. And according to this section of the draft annual report, it is also stated that the president of the government, that is, the prime minister, had received over 90 different documents from the RS MUP and that the president and the members of the Presidency had received more than 80 documents of an analytical nature in the course of the past eight months.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, if I could just go back to page 7 of the English. And I think it's on page 6 of the B/C/S. You mentioned earlier about the activities regarding the division of the MUP. In the last paragraph on page 7 of the English, is this what's discussed?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think this particular paragraph of the draft 1992 RS MUP annual report is quite significant and is also, again, corroborated by many other documents produced by the RS MUP in the course of 1992 and subsequently. I want to preface my comments on this paragraph with the fact that I'm not a lawyer and I'm not taking any position whatsoever on the veracity or accuracy of the statements being made by the RS MUP as to legal or illegal actions. However, as an analyst I find it highly relevant to note that in the 1992 draft annual report of the RS Ministry of Internal Affairs, and indeed in many other documents of the RS MUP in 1992 and indeed in later years, they refer to their own actions, particularly for the period prior to April 1992, as "illegal." I want to very clearly stress that this is their word; it is not mine. And it appears in the original of these documents. Here in this particular paragraph we see that they talk about the illegal organisation of the Serbian Ministry of Internal Affairs, the illegal arming of reliable active personnel and reserve employees, and indeed at another point in the report they point out that the Bosnian Serbs in the Ministry of Internal Affairs, at a time when there was still a joint multi-ethnic Bosnian Ministry of Internal Affairs, engaged in the - again in their own words - "illegal" arming of Serbs in municipalities under the control of the SDS at that time. They also refer to unilateral actions, including combat activities undertaken by Bosnian Serbs over half a year before the Bosnian Serbs established their own Ministry of Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could go to the following --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have a reference for the line and could we also have the -- could we see the actual exhibit that has been admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a draft. So first of all, can I have a reference what line this was in, and then we have the separate issue of the document. But I'd like to see the line where the word "illegal" is used.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's inappropriate. This document has been admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just -- the Witness, answer this question without indicating specific passage in this report, did he?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, Dr. Nielsen referred to illegal organisation of the Serbian MUP and illegal -- this reference to illegal arming. It's on the second line of the last paragraph of page 6 of the English. And in the B/C/S it's on page -- sorry, page 10 of the -- it's -- it's numbered page 6 of the B/C/S in the actual document but it's page 10 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we can go to page 7 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Very quickly, Dr. Nielsen -- and so it would be page -- it's also on the same page and then going over on to the up -- the next page of the B/C/S. We see a lot of numbers there in relation to personnel of the Serbian MUP. Do you have a comment to make briefly about those figures?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could go to the following page of the English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I would note two things about the numbers that are stated on personnel in the draft 1992 annual report of the RS MUP. First and foremost, I would note that the RS MUP increased greatly in size. The size of the RS MUP alone was much larger because -- particularly because of the size of the reserve police force in the summer of 1992 than its predecessor, the SRBH MUP had been. And second of all, as I note in examining this draft 1992 annual report, there is an extremely extensive involvement of the ministry in combat activities. Here we see a figure that is given well over 300.000 days of man -- man days, so to speak, of combat involvement or on average 1.451 police officers per day for every day from April to December 1992 involved in combat on the part of the RS MUP.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to turn now to talk about -- to discuss the RS MUP involvement in detention facilities. In paragraph 296 of your report you say that: "By mid-July 1992 at the latest, all leading officials of the RS MUP were fully aware of the ministry's involvement in the operation of detention camps."

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In -- on 11 July 1992, the entire leadership of the RS MUP met in Belgrade together with one representative of the federal secretariat for internal affairs in Belgrade and discussed the work of the ministry and the challenges and problems confronting the ministry. One of the items clearly discussed at that meeting was the involvement of the employees of the ministry in the operation and guarding of detention facilities in the RS. This particularly came out in the comments of Stojan Zupljanin, who was the chief of the CSB in Banja Luka and who noted that the police were guarding large numbers of Muslims and that in some of these camps the conditions were inadequate.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I would note that this is -- the 65 ter number 09243 is in fact Exhibit D00447.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would just note that I stated that the conditions were inadequate and not inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What other major issues were discussed at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Other major issues discussed at this meeting were the extensive involvement of the police in armed combat activities. Memorably quoted by one key participant who stated that it was unacceptable that the police were in the trenches when the army was guarding or was checking traffic, that it should be the other way around. So the police definitely were unsatisfied with the extent of their combat involvement. They discussed co-operation with civilian authorities and in particular difficulties in co-ordinating with various Crisis Staffs. They discussed the challenges facing the police in dealing with paramilitary organisations. They discussed the role of the police in, in their own words, in defending the territory of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And they discussed the types of rules and regulations that needed to be elaborated and promulgated in the months to come. I would note that the aversion of the notes of this meeting, the minutes of this meeting, as well as a document dated 17 July 1992, in which the main findings of the meeting were enunciated, were distributed to the higher RS authorities, in particular the prime minister and the president of the Presidency, Dr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You mentioned that they discuss at this meeting the various challenges facing the police dealing with the paramilitary organisations, and there's a section on the relationship between the RS MUP and the paramilitary organisations at -- in paragraphs 361 and 378 of your report.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask to seek leave to use Defence Exhibit D01412, which is a report by Milorad Davidovic. It was not on our list because it was exhibited only at the same time as the final notification was being filed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think there's any opposition from the Defence. Yes, proceed, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If that could be brought up on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Exhibit number is 142?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, have you had an opportunity to review this document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I reviewed this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It indicates that Mr. Davidovic was sent in to clean up the problems associated with some paramilitary groups. What were these problems?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As indicated in this and other documents, a large number of paramilitary groups, many of them stemming from the territory of Serbia, entered the territory of the Serbian Republic, that is to say the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, beginning in April 1992 and participated in operations, combat operations, but also engaged extensively, as we see in this document, in activities that are described by the police and by Mr. Davidovic as being illegal, particularly looting but also killings and in some cases other types of violence against civilians and others. By the time of the 11 July meeting to which I referred previously, the RS MUP was increasingly of the opinion that these paramilitary formations should no longer be allowed to operate. However, they in most cases conditioned their opposition to these paramilitary formations, as does indeed Mr. Davidovic in this document, with an appreciation in their opinion of the assistance that these paramilitary formations had offered in the take-over of authority in various regions of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And the focus -- the focus was therefore from the point of view of the police on integrating units, paramilitary units, if at all possible, into regular units, particularly of the Army of the RS; or if that was impossible, if the groups were deemed too violent or too criminal in nature, then they should be expelled to the territory of Serbia. This resulted, as I detail in my section on paramilitary organisations, particularly in paragraphs 365 and following, in a large operation at the end of July 1992 where the RS MUP expelled the Yellow Wasps, a paramilitary formation also mentioned in the document in front of us from the territory of Zvornik municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: But how did these groups, including the Yellow Wasps, come to be in BiH in the first place?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly when these groups were arrested - and I have been able to review a large number of statements which are footnoted in footnote 567 of my report of paramilitary members that were arrested and gave statements to the RS police, in the words of these paramilitary members, the reason why they were in the -- in Bosnia and Herzegovina was because they had come to defend the Serbian nation. A number of the paramilitary members who were arrested by the police expressed strong disbelief. They simply did not understand why they had been arrested, given that they had been co-operating with the police just a few weeks earlier. And in at least one case, one of the paramilitary members whose statement is -- was taken by the RS MUP and is footnoted in footnote 567, stated that he had come to help assist the Serbian cause in Bosnia and Herzegovina after reading an appeal by Dr. Nikola Koljevic, who was a member of the Presidency of the Serbian Republic. Most of these people stemmed from the territory of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, did any of these -- these people from the groups have any meetings with members of the RS Presidency?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In these same statements, in a number of these statements, there are references to a meeting with Biljana Plavsic in Pale in the summer of 1992, where these paramilitaries went for what they deemed an informal meeting with Ms. Plavsic. Again, the fact that these paramilitary members had only weeks earlier been co-operating with the police and with the army and indeed had met with high-level members of the Bosnian Serb leadership led these paramilitaries to be bewildered by the fact that they were now being arrested and expelled from the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. Dr. Nielsen, I wanted to take you to paragraph -- on another topic, to paragraph 298 of your report, where you talk about the processing of detainees and the categorisation of these detainees. From the police's own documents, what was the categorisation? What was their categorisation of the detainees?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the middle of the summer of 1992, the RS MUP was detaining thousands of persons according to their own documents in various detention facilities, particularly in north-western Bosnia and Herzegovina on the territory under the jurisdiction of CSB Banja Luka. At -- as partial result of the 11 July meeting, there was a decision to try to figure out who these people actually were and whether they should still be detained because, as previously noted, Mr. Zupljanin in Banja Luka had indicated that these people had been detained en masse by the Crisis Staffs and the army, according to his words, and that they had been "dumped" upon the police who were being forced to deal with these large numbers of people in detention facilities. So they devised a system of categories, which I describe in paragraph 298. And according to this the first category would be people in these detention facilities who were suspected of committing criminal acts. The second was comprised of persons suspected of aiding and abetting those who committed criminal acts. And the third category was comprised of "adult males concerning whom the service has not to date gathered any security-relevant data on the basis of which these persons may be treated as hostages." After that report, a discussion ensued, which I describe in paragraphs 298 through 302 of my report, both involving members of the government and the Presidency but also varying opinions within the police about what should actually be done with these people, particularly because it emerged over time that the largest category of persons seem to be in this third category.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have Exhibit Number 09453 -- sorry, 65 ter number 09453 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, this is an -- in appendix B, document 13. It's the SJB Prijedor report of January 1993. Does that document make reference to the categorisation of the detainees? And just, first of all, before we get there. In relation to the Prijedor municipality, what was the level of involvement of the police in camps in that municipality?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: To answer that question, I would refer to page 5 and the following pages of the B/C/S, in which the Prijedor police themselves describe their extensive involvement in operating three so-called collection centres, one being Keraterm, one being Trnopolje, and one being Omarska --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It would be beneficial on the part of the Chamber to follow. Could you wait.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So are we on the correct page? Yes, please proceed, Dr. Nielsen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. As the Chamber will see at the bottom of this page in -- on the English, it says that three collection centres were established on the territory of Prijedor municipality, Keraterm, Trnopolje, and Omarska. And it says that several thousand people passed through these centres and that about 6.000 preliminary interviews were conducted with these people. It was on the basis of such interviews, which I would note were conducted usually with -- in co-operation with the military but within the police by both the national and Public Security Service. It was in the course of such discussions that decisions were made about who fit into which category of these three categories that I referred to earlier.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And while we have that document up on the screen, is there any reference in that document to whether the actions of the Bosnian Serbs were illegal?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on the second page of the B/C/S - and here I want to make clear that this doesn't -- these comments that I'm about to make refer to other activities, not the detention facilities' related activities, but to activities taken at earlier stages. It notes that preparations for the establishment of the take-over of the police by the Serbs in Prijedor municipality had to be undertaken in a covert and, in their words, illegal manner. It refers to the illegal organisation and formation of shadow police stations, because at the time the SDA, that is, the Bosnian Muslim party, controlled a large number of people in the police in the municipality. And therefore, the Bosnian Serbs had to act covertly in making their plans to take-over the police in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be, yes, admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2968, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Exhibit P2968.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Also in paragraph 288 of your statement when you were discussing the detention centres in Prijedor you cite to two exhibits P02460 and P2793, which I won't -- won't call up at the moment. What part, if any, did the National Security Service play in relation to the detention facilities?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The National Security Service, which was of course part of RS MUP -- and I should state so that it is clear was named the National Security Service. It was what had earlier been known in Bosnia as the State Security Service and was indeed after 1994 again renamed the State Security Service in the RS as well. This National Security Service in 1992 was charged with protecting the security of the Bosnian Serb state and its constitutional order. And along those lines, it engaged in the interrogation of persons who were detained on suspicion of having conducted activities aimed at toppling the Serbian Republic or resisting the imposition of the authority of the Serbian Republic. And it's confirmed -- I deal with that, for example, in paragraph 289, that the National Security Service, abbreviated SNB, had conducted a total of over 8.000 "informational interviews" with a total of 5.740 persons in detention facilities in a number of municipalities. As I note elsewhere in my report, particularly in the section dealing with the National Security Service, it is clear that the National Security Service was also aware that a large number of persons of Bosnian Croat and Bosnian Muslim ethnicity were leaving north-western Bosnia-Herzegovina and that there was a level of destruction of religious buildings, mosques, churches, et cetera, that was also taking place during this period.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Just going back to the reference you made to paragraph 289 and the number of people that were informally -- sorry, that were interviewed, informational interviews, you also note in paragraph 289 that: "However, a total of only four criminal complaints were filed by these authorities during that year." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what the document states. Certainly, looking at all of these documents in total, as an analyst, there is a significant disparity between the number of the number of persons who were detained in these facilities, which often goes up, as the Court can see, to the thousands of persons, and the very, very small number of persons who were eventually charged with any criminal acts.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You mentioned earlier on in your testimony a meeting of the 17th of July - and this is 65 ter number 01587 which is Exhibit P01096 - and you said a copy of that report was provided to the president of the Presidency and the prime minister. What was actually dealt with at this meeting on the 17th of July, very briefly?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to put in a small correction because there was no meeting as such on the 17th of July. The 17 July document that we see in front of us is merely an information about the most significant findings and conclusions of the meeting that took place in Belgrade on the 11th of July, 1992. As we see on the cover page of the 17 July document, it was -- in the Serbian it's in -- it's handwritten that the report was delivered to the president of the Presidency and to the prime minister. And it contained all of the key findings on all of the topics that I earlier noted had been discussed at the 11 July meeting, including the topic of what to do with the large numbers of people who were detained in those detention facilities.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In paragraphs 301 and 302 of your report, you indicate that the Republika Srpska authorities had to deal with detention facilities because of an increasingly -- an increasing number of international complaints. How did they deal with -- how did they deal with this?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a matter of general knowledge that by the middle of July 1992, the existence of detention facilities, particularly in north-western Bosnia and Herzegovina, had become known both in Bosnia and Herzegovina and internationally. As a result of this, in the following weeks after this 11 July meeting, pressure rose to disband these detention facilities but the police discussed at length what was actually to be done with these people who were detained in such facilities. In the event, as I discuss in the subsequent paragraphs of my report, the tendency was to transfer -- to close the facilities, such as Omarska, that were being operated by the police and which had been established pursuant to Crisis Staff orders and to move most of the people who were being kept at such facilities to facilities under the control of the military, in particular the Manjaca detention facility in -- also in north-western Bosnia and Herzegovina. And I discuss that in paragraphs 291, 292, and 293, particularly in the light of the fact that according to documentation of the Army of Republika Srpska, they were quite -- that is to say, the receiving officers of the Army of Republika Srpska were quite astonished and very displeased by the state in which these people were being transferred to their custody at Manjaca. Criticisms made by the military of the police's handling of these persons included complaints that no adequate dossiers accompanied these prisoners, so it was difficult to see why they had been detained in the first place. And secondly, in a number of cases, which I deal with in the paragraphs that I just mentioned, officers of the VRS complained that prisoners or persons who were being transferred to Manjaca from Omarska had been physically beaten and in some cases even killed by the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did Mr. Karadzic issue any orders in relation to persons being detained?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am aware of the fact, and I cite on several occasions in the report, that during the course of the summer of 1992 on repeated occasions the -- Dr. Karadzic, as the president of the Presidency, issued orders encouraging -- or I should say ordering subordinates to treat all persons detained according to the Geneva Conventions. I cite one example of such a document on the 23rd of July in paragraph 299, and as I note elsewhere such documents or such orders, that the Geneva Conventions should be respected, were issued also later during the course of August. In paragraph 310 I note a 19 August order by Dr. Karadzic to the VRS and the MUP to treat all prisoners in accordance with international norms.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: On the 23rd of July, 1992, the order you just referred to of Mr. Karadzic, was there any conditional -- conditions put on that order? I think that's 65 ter number 11100. Do you recall if there was any conditional language?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the 23rd July 1992 order, Dr. Karadzic seemed to condition -- in the first paragraph of that order seemed to condition the implementation -- let me just make sure that we have the right document here. Could I have paragraph 1 of the B/C/S enlarged, please. My reading of this document, the B/C/S language of the document -- and I would note that it's an incomplete translation on the English version of the order. But my reading of the first paragraph of this document seemed to indicate that there was some conditionality in the observation of the Geneva Conventions in Dr. Karadzic's mind, particularly conditioning the respect of the Geneva Conventions to that portion of the population which did not resist the authority of the RS or engage in combat activities against the RS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In your opinion, how should English translation be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I -- again, is it possible for the Serbian to be enlarged even larger than present? Or for me to have the original because it's very difficult to read on the screen, but I'll give it my best try. As I read it, it says: "Towards the civilian population of any nationality which does not display," I believe it's -- but it's very difficult to see on the screen, it was much easier when I had the printed document I was looking at earlier, "that does not display aggression and combat activities towards our army and towards the civilian population of the Serbian authority, one must treat them in accordance with the law and with the Geneva Conventions." What I meant by the conditionality here is that it seems to be conditioning the observation of the Geneva Conventions on whether or not the civilian population accepts Serbian rule or resists it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: So would the English translation be incorrect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because as you see there's a passage there, Your Honour, that is referred to as illegible, and that to me is the crucial part that's missing from that -- that paragraph. Because the -- it's not regarding the civilian population of any ethnicity, full stop. It's regarding the civilian population of any ethnicity that does not participate in resistance or combat activities towards our army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You mentioned a moment ago that there was also another order by Karadzic on the 19th of August, 1992. When was the international community focusing on the detention facilities, do you know?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know that by the 2nd of August, and that is to say by the beginning of August, and I referred to some of the international journalists in footnotes 431 and 432, news articles had started to be published internationally focusing on what was allegedly the mistreatment of persons detained in these facilities. So, as I said, after that happened this trend seemed to reinforce the desire of the RS MUP to divest itself of, as it were, the business of detaining large numbers of persons. And we see a quite accelerated push during the month of August, 1992, to shut down detention facilities operated by the RS MUP and to transfer people detained in those facilities either to territories outside of the Serbian Republic or, in some cases, to the jurisdiction of the VRS, particularly at the detention facility of Manjaca operated by the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I note the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll have a break for half an hour and resume at five past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Just before the break, Dr. Nielsen, you mentioned that -- that there was quite a push during the month of August to shut down the detention facility operated by the RS MUP and to transfer people detained in those facilities to either the territories outside of the Serbian territory or in some cases to the jurisdiction of the RS, i.e., Manjaca. According to the RS MUP's own documentation, were there any instances in which abuse was committed against the persons who had been detained in these detention facilities who were being transferred elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to the RS MUP's own documentation, there were such instances. I deal with one of those in I believe paragraphs -- I'll just locate that. In paragraphs, for example, 327, where there was one transport of persons who had been detained at one police-controlled facility and there was an incident which was described as being a "massacre" and where the VRS urged that the police engage in investigation of that incident which had taken place while the convoy was under police jurisdiction.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And is that the incident known as either the Koricani Stijena or the Mount Vlasic massacre?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the incident which has been referred to at this Tribunal and elsewhere Koricanska Stijena incident.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You mention in paragraph 327 of the report that Zupljanin who was the chief of the CSB was asking Drljaca, who was chief of the Prijedor SJB, to carry out an investigation immediately. And there's a reference to Drljaca responding, they couldn't be carried out because the officers were deployed on the battle-field.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter number 05781 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: That doesn't appear to be the correct document. 05781.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And while we're waiting for that --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, I see we have the correct B/C/S but the English translation doesn't appear to be the same document. Okay. We have the right one now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Was that the document that you were referring to in paragraph 327?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And the fact that the policemen that were involved in the escort on the Travnik convoy on the 21st of August, 1992, are at the front, what can you tell us about policemen going to the front after -- sorry, after they may have been involved in certain incidents?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there's two points here. One specifically relating to this incident which is that when Drljaca on the 14th of September says that these officers cannot be investigated because they're deployed at the battle-field, his superior, Stojan Zupljanin, again seeks information but there's no indication, certainly in 1992, that any investigation was pursued on this matter despite the very strong words of the army in describing what took place during that incident. At a more general level, the minister of internal affairs in the summer of 1992, Mico Stanisic, made reference and indeed ordered that those police officers who had been committing infractions which were incompatible with their service in the police should be transferred to serve in the Army of Republika Srpska. That is, instead of removing them entirely from service, they would instead end up serving in the military. And indeed the draft 1992 annual report of the RS MUP by and large confirms that many thousands of police were in the course of 1992 transferred to military service, a much larger number than the number of police officers against whom disciplinary or criminal proceedings were pursued.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender that document that's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2969, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And I also, Your Honour, before the break I seeked to tender the document that Dr. Nielsen referred to in relation to Mr. Karadzic's order of the 23rd of July, 1992, and that's 65 ter number 0 -- 11100.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: About which Dr. Nielsen indicated that the English translation is not complete?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And that was a draft translation and the final translation will reflect the correct English translation?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I will see to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, that will be admitted as well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2970, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could have a document that's listed in appendix B, 65 ter number 21837. It's document 12 in that appendix.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is this the document you were referring to a moment ago when you said that Mico Stanisic issued an order in the summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is that order.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2971.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I want to turn now to discuss deportations, and this matter is dealt with in paragraphs 320 to 329 of your report. What role did the RS MUP play in the deportations or expulsions of the non-Serb population?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on my review of the RS MUP's own documentation for the summer of 1992 and the autumn of 1992, it is clear that the police in co-operation with the Crisis Staffs and also in co-operation with the military first established and then guarded detention facilities that I referred to earlier where large numbers of people were detained. As I noted earlier in my testimony today, there was a tendency that once these facilities in the late summer and early autumn of 1992 were being disbanded, the persons who were in those facilities did not return to their residences, but instead had to leave the territory under the control of the RS, many of them ending up elsewhere in the former Yugoslavia, for example, in Croatia or abroad. I would also note that a number of persons of course who were never detained in detention facilities were -- went straight from their residences in various parts of territory under the control of the Bosnian Serbs to territories outside Bosnia-Herzegovina. In many cases, the police played a facilitating role in this process.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You note in paragraph 320 of your report that the police would regulate the departures in co-operation with the municipal secretariat for national defence. And you also talk about the voluntariness or involuntariness of this action in paragraph 320. Were the police making any comments as to whether they could guarantee these persons' safety or not if they were to stay in the -- on the territory?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a number of cases I reviewed documents in which the police and/or the Crisis Staffs were -- I would again remind that the police were a constituent part of the Crisis Staffs - issued statements to the effect that the physical security of persons who were detained in detention facilities could not be guaranteed if they returned to their residences nor could the security of their property be guaranteed. I note in paragraph 326 of my report that Vinko Kondic, who was the chief of police in the SJB Kljuc, reported that pressure had been put on Muslims to leave Kljuc municipality. And while noting that Muslims had started what he called an armed rebellion against Serbian rule, he also observed that they had been the objects of what he called a campaign of terror with "monstrous crimes being committed against the Muslims." In some cases these crimes were perpetrated by people who were either police officers or wearing uniforms of various kinds. I would also note that in paragraph 321 there was a reference in the RS MUP daily bulletin to an extraordinary event in July 1992 in Sokolac municipality, on the other side of the Serbian Republic, where an entire Muslim family that had actually declared its loyalty to the RS authorities was killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter number 00883 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is the dispatch of the SJB Kljuc dated the 28th of September, 1992. Is that the document that you just referred to?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the document that I cite in paragraph 326 of my report.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is not related to the event noted in para 321?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: 326, Your Honour, I'm sorry, Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2972, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Could we see next page or how many pages this document has?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Two pages. And I note there on page 2 it says the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just going back to para 321, you noted that while the authorities attempted to ensure that equal protection was provided, the -- that example referred to in that paragraph shows the contrary. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is one example where it appears that despite assertions made on repeated occasions that all persons who declared their loyalty to the Serbian Republic would be able to live under complete physical security on the territory of the RS, unfortunately the contrary occurred and the RS MUP, in fact, reported that it was very deplorable that a family of Bosnian Muslims who had declared their loyalty was killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So does it mean, in your opinion, that authorities didn't attempt to ensure that equal protection was provided?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would not like to generalise on that point. What does appear to take place over the summer of 1992 is that there are a number of places in which the police seems - and it varies from case to case - unwilling or unable to provide for the security of Bosnian Muslims and Bosnian Croats who remain on the territory of the RS. And certainly, in such cases where crimes against such persons are committed, it is difficult to see that due diligence was exercised in terms of investigating and prosecuting those crimes, which links to a subsequent point that I make in the report in paragraphs 327 and elsewhere, that there is at times a disparity in the documentation of the RS MUP itself between the level of emphasis placed on the investigation of what they termed war crimes against Serbs and war crimes against others. There are cases in which the minister of internal affairs says, full stop, that all war crimes or allegations of war crimes should be investigated thoroughly; but there are also several occasions on which both he and the civilian authorities of the RS tend to emphasize the investigation of war crimes committed against the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, I think you deal with this in paragraphs 3 -- 236 and 237; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So in your view, was there a pattern established in relation to the non-Serb civilians by the RS MUP authorities or by the authorities generally?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the most nuanced way of phrasing it is that despite repeated assertions by both the political and police authorities of the RS, that they would seek to provide full security for all citizens of the Serbian Republic, regardless of ethnicity, the documentation of the police itself shows cumulatively that in many, many cases such security was not provided to Bosnian Muslims and Bosnian Croats and that the consequences of violent acts against the persons and property of Bosnian Muslims and Bosnian Croats in the course of the summer of 1992 were not prioritised as a matter of investigation by the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I want to just deal briefly with reports of the MUP about their involvement in events in 1992. We've discussed on a number of occasions the draft report, and that's dealt with in paragraphs 379 to 391 of your report. I want to take you to the work report of the RS MUP Romanija Birac CSB.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And that's 65 ter number 11528. And English page 3 and B/C/S page 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What is the significance of this document, and in particular references to the SDS?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cite this report in footnote 597 on page 109 of my report, noting that this report of CSB Sarajevo emphasises that the SDS was regarded by the police for the duration of 1992 in the RS as the bearer of the activities and means for the liberation of the Serbian nation. The organs of internal affairs, so to say, first entered into the battle of the Serbian nation for liberation. So this ties together two of my earlier points; one, the identification by the Bosnian Serb police with the political programmes of the Serbian Democratic Party; and secondly, the prominent and indeed leading role, particularly in the first half -- month and a half of the conflict in Bosnia and Herzegovina that the police itself played. As I note in paragraph 383 where footnote 597 is located, this goes all the way back -- one can trace such associations between the Bosnian Serbs in the police and the SDS all the way back to 1991, where again the police in their draft 1992 annual report state that already in the second half of 1991 and early 1992 Serbs had -- Serbs in the police had been "illegally," again their word, illegally arming Serbian civilians in municipalities that were at that point under the control of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You also discuss in paragraph 70 and 71, 72 an SJB Ilidza report, which is 65 ter number 01230, now Exhibit P02308, and that is on appendix A, document number 25. And you state in your report that there is co-ordination -- and this is a document -- the SJB Ilidza report is dated the 20th of September, 1993, but it makes reference to the co-ordination of the Serbs prior to April 1992, does it not?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. This is one of a considerable number of reports from the second half of 1993 that are retrospective in nature. The reason for these reports is that there was at the time an attempt to nominate deserving individuals of the RS MUP for high distinctions and awards and medals by the Bosnian Serb leadership, and these documents at length enunciate the reasons for why various persons in the police from the municipal level all the way up to the top of the ministry should receive such awards. And indeed they were subsequently awarded awards by Dr. Karadzic, as the president of the RS, in I believe November 1993. As I referred to in paragraph 72 of my report, here and also paragraph 71, we once again here in these nomination texts see that the police perceive it to be a -- laudable that the police as early as 1991 co-operated closely with SDS representatives and acted on the directives of the SDS. These nomination texts very frequently -- or commendation I suppose would be the better word, commendation texts frequently refer to, again in their own words, illegal activities that the police was engaged in prior to 1992. And in the case of Mr. Tomislav Kovac, who was before the war commander of the police in Ilidza in a suburb of Sarajevo and who later rose to become minister of internal affairs in 1995, one commendation described him as having organised "the formation of the Serbian public security station, organising illegal work and the arming of the Serbian people" and they also commended him for ensuring that Croats and Muslims were removed from the Ilidza police station before the war even began.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And that is Exhibit P02308 that I just mentioned a moment ago, Your Honour, so I won't bring it up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Were you minded to tender that --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, I was just about to make an --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's Romanija Birac CSB work report, that will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2973, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You mentioned Mr. Karadzic awarding RS MUP with awards. If I could have 65 ter number 05289 on the screen, please. And this is the document that you just referred to in paragraph 72 of your report and you said November 1993. If we look at -- one moment. We can see that this is a decree adopted by the president of the Republika Srpska on awarding commendations. And if we look at the first article, can you just look at the persons listed 1 to 5, and do you have any comment in relation to those persons listed there?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, the highest commendation, the Nemanjic order, is awarded to the ministry as a whole and then to four individuals who were all playing leading roles in the formation of RS MUP and indeed in its operations during 1992. In many cases again there are documents of the police themselves in which these persons are thanked for playing leading roles in the establishment of the Serbian Republic and in the defence of that republic. Often, again, in the police's own words, they proudly use the term "illegal" to refer to activities that these people undertook prior to April 1992. The document as a whole beyond these first couple of individuals is a veritable who is who of RS MUP in 1992. I would note that Simo Drljaca, who was the chief of police in -- in Prijedor as well as his commander, Stojan Zupljanin, appear on the following page as receiving the Karadjordjevic star 1st class commendation. And perhaps it is also worth noting that in the case of some of the individuals who received commendations, these were even individuals who had been criticised within the RS MUP for playing disruptive roles, in particular Ljuban Ecim who had been the leader of the special police in the Banja Luka area.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You mentioned that -- you mentioned Tomo Kovac as the minister of the MUP. What position did he hold in 1992?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tomislav Kovac at the beginning of the war was the commander of the police at SJB Ilidza. He was then promoted to chief of police in Ilidza, and as I, in fact, note in my report on the section on the paramilitary operations, in August 1992 his rise through the ranks of the police continued only actually a day or two after he had recommended that the police continue to engage in joint operations with an indeed armed paramilitary groups which, in principle, should have been disbanded by that point. He was then appointed, I believe it's stated in my report, in August 1992 to the position of assistant minister, and by the time we get to 1995 he was acting minister of -- or, excuse me, deputy minister and indeed acting minister during the summer of 1995 for RS MUP. And subsequently he was promoted to minister of RS MUP, a position he held until December 1995, when he was replaced by Dragan Kijac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could go to page 2 of the document and still on page 1 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And you mentioned a moment ago Simo Drljaca who you said was chief of the police in Prijedor. And you noted in I think paragraph 327 of your report that it was -- the Prijedor the police were involved in the Koricani Stijena massacre; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, both according to the documents of the RS MUP and of the VRS. And I would just supplement my previous answer by noting that it is in paragraph 374 of my report that I refer to Kovac's promotion in August 1992 to assistant minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And Stojan Zupljanin, what did he -- was he promoted throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Stojan Zupljanin, who had been the chief of the CSB in Banja Luka from already 1991 was, I believe, in 1994 promoted to be the advisor to the president of the RS on security matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And you mentioned Ljuban Ecim. If we could go to page 3 of the English and page 2 of the B/C/S. And Ljuban Ecim and Zdravko Samardzija, listed at number 6 and 7 for the Karadjordjevic star 3rd class.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I would note for the Court that in the section of my report starting around paragraph 223 on page 67, I deal in length or at length with the formation of the CSB Banja Luka special police unit which was commanded by Ljubomir Ecim and in which Mr. Samardzija also served.
