This was a unit that had its origins as a Serbian paramilitary unit and which during the course of 1992 in the summer engaged in a number of activities that were regarded as callous and highly problematic by the -- by many civilian and indeed police authorities in the region, which led therefore that special police unit to be partially disbanded in August 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You mentioned a moment ago that there was MUP supporting documentation for these nominations for commendations. And these are listed on appendix B and these are discussed at paragraph 71 and 72 of your report.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And they're 65 ter numbers 018 -- sorry, my mistake, 18264, which is entitled: "RS MUP Nominations for Commendation." Another document, 65 ter number 10416 which is an undated commendation for Srecko Samardzija. Another document, 65 ter number 01671 from the Blazuj reserve police SJB proposal for public recognition. And 65 ter number 11302, which is dealt with at paragraph 72 which is RS MUP notice concerning the activities of the reserve militia station in Ilidza, which is undated. Are they the documents that you were referring to a moment ago when you said there was supporting documentation?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is part of the supporting documentation. I would stress that unfortunately I was not able to locate supporting documentation for all of the persons nominated in -- for presidential awards in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender those four documents without the need to call them up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I have to ask the opinion of Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection. Since he's described them generally, it's okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, given the position of the Defence, we'll admit these documents. Yes, we give the numbers for these.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, they will be Exhibits P2974 through P2977.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Witness -- Dr. Nielsen referred to his report paragraph 327, the parts referring to Drljaca. Could you go through with him what that -- the paragraph refers to.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, we dealt with that I think just after the break when we were talking about the Koricani Stijena and the order from Zupljanin to Drljaca to investigate the matter, and then Drljaca responded to Zupljanin: Well, they're off at the front in Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Have we admitted those documents?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And the VRS report as well?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I can -- I can locate the army document to see whether in fact it is admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And could you tell me the exhibit number of the documents we admitted -- I mean the MUP documents. Please proceed in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The dispatch from Drljaca back to Zupljanin on the 14th of September, 1992, is Exhibit P2969.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, I think the army document that you referred to earlier in your testimony was dated the 21st or the 22nd of August, was it not?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I refer, actually, to a number of VRS combat reports and other documents in paragraph 327 that deal with this incident. So footnotes 496 and 497 and also there is a press conference with General-Major Talic in 495.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can give you the 65 ter numbers for those documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I have the footnote.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And could I tender the presidential decree on the distribution of awards, 65 ter number 05289, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2978, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, I wish to turn to another topic now, and that is the topic of Typhoon and Sigma. The Court was directed to an exhibit the other day, Exhibit P0296.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And I would seek leave to use this exhibit, Your Honour. If that could be brought up on to the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did he deal with it in his report?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Uh, no, Your Honour. And this is the public version of the document. If we could have the following page.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an Official Note of the 2nd Administration of the State Security Service of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Serbian Republic dated 27 June 1994, connected to the group known as Typhoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And there's a reference in the document to Sigma.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Essentially there was an intelligence group whose origins go all the way back to the second half of 1991, to the JNA, who during the course of 1991 and 1992 organised themselves and proffered their services to the authorities of the Serbian Republic and were constituted as information centre Typhoon, I believe, in June 1992 pursuant to an order by the president of the republic, Dr. Karadzic. This group was subsequently engaged in a number of activities of a controversial nature, with the result that efforts were made by the authorities of the RS to disband the information centre Typhoon. And here we see in this document from June 1994 that members of this former group decided to establish contact directly with the State Security Service of the Republic of Serbia, where they are now proffering their services to Belgrade, as it were. And a decision is made here by the deputy chief of administration - I note that his name is redacted here - that the deputy chief of information in the Serbian State Security Service agrees that these persons should be allowed to enter into service for the Serbian State Security Service and that they shall be constituted under the pseudonym Sigma.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You mentioned a moment ago that Typhoon was constituted as an information centre pursuant to an order of the president of the republic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to add an exhibit 65 ter number 23182 and to use that with Dr. Nielsen. It is in relation to the establishment of the group Typhoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We did receive notice recently that they were going to seek to add these to the 65 ter list and we don't object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Granted.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If 65 ter number 23182 could be brought up on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is a decision dated the 22nd of July, 1992. Was this the decision that you spoke of a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe there -- if memory serves - and it's been a while since I looked at all the documents - but I believe there's even an earlier document. I think I referred to June 1992. But in any case this certainly shows that in July 1992 Dr. Karadzic in his capacity as the president of the National Security Council in the RS is asking for the army of the Serbian Republic and the MUP to co-operate with the information centre Typhoon in its operations.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And I note that the broad number is 01-343/92.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, this will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2979, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And if I could go to another document related to Typhoon which is 65 ter number 23183, also disclosed, as Mr. Robinson said, as a potential 65 ter exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, this is a document dated the 30th of November, 1992, signed by the president, Dr. Karadzic, and it's an order referring to an order of the 23rd of June, 1992, with the broad number 01-140/92. Do you have any comment on this document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I believe that that number, 01-140/92, is most likely the document from June 1992 that I was referring to earlier, but again this document which is, in this case, issued by Dr. Karadzic in his capacity as president of the Presidency of the RS, states again that the information centre Typhoon exists and that it is supposed to be enjoying the protection of the 1st Krajina Corps in the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And you said that Typhoon then became -- then was working under the -- the pseudonym of Sigma. And then you said that it was disbanded by the authorities of the RS because of -- it was engaged in a number of activities of a controversial nature. Can you just briefly describe why it was disbanded.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just want to clarify that Typhoon was disbanded -- at least attempts were made to put it out of existence in 1993 and late -- early 1994, but that it resurfaced, now under the protection of Serbian state security and allegedly with the permission of the RS authorities, in June 1994 as Sigma. So there was nothing called Sigma until the summer of 1994. The reason that Typhoon or one of the reasons that Typhoon was disbanded was that it turned out that among its activities were intelligence reports that were produced on allegedly very high levels of corruption among persons either in the Bosnian Serb leadership or close to that leadership. That was not something that was desirable from the point of view of the Bosnian Serb authorities, and that was according to many sources the reason -- one of the reasons why Typhoon was being shut down.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I've finished with that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I wish to deal now with another topic, the period from mid-1995. Did the hierarchical structure of the RS MUP change between 1993 and mid-1995?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The essential structure of the ministry remained the same, although there were a number of smaller, I would say, cosmetic changes made to the titles of various units and entities within the RS MUP. One of them that I referred to earlier was the renaming of the National Security Service as the State Security Service.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Who was the minister of the MUP in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe his name was, if memory serves, Zivko Rakic, but it may have been Ratic, Ratic or Rakic. But at any rate he was not the one who on a daily basis was actually running the ministry at that point.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Who was the deputy minister?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tomislav Kovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Who was head of the public security?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milenko Karisik.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Who was the head of the state security?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dragan Kijac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the special police brigade?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Goran Saric.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And who was his deputy?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ljubomir Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, I'm not going to get into the substance of the Srebrenica operation with you, but I do want to ask you a few questions about how the RS MUP was structured and how it was operating during the period June/July 1995. And I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before doing so, you're tendering that previous Typhoon document?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Putting under the 1st Krajina Corps. That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2980, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You mentioned a moment ago that Rakic -- or you said Ratic or Rakic was not the one who was on a daily basis running the ministry at that point. I was going to deal with it a little later, but at this point who was dealing with it? Who was running the ministry at that point in 1995?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of the documentation from June and July 1995 indicates that on a de facto basis the person issuing orders, instructions, et cetera, in the RS MUP was Tomislav Kovac, the deputy minister. He subsequently became minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Now, the questions that I want to -- the topics that I want to ask you about relate to the following, and that's the establishment of the Pale police staff, the relationship between the RS MUP and the Serbian MUP units operating in the Republika Srpska. I will ask you some questions about Tomo Kovac's positions in July 1995 and the reporting by the subordinate units to him and communications between state security and other units. I want to also take you to an example of how the MUP implemented an order from the president during this period, and I will also be asking you to identify the names and positions of RS MUP members who appear in Mr. Karadzic's appointment diary in this period.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would seek leave to add a document to the 65 ter list and that's Exhibit 23166. It was disclosed to the Defence on the 14th of March, 2011, under Rule 68(ii) and on the 22nd of June, 2011, as a potential 65 ter exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If that document could be brought up on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: First of all, Dr. Nielsen, were you aware -- are you aware of a police staff command being set up in Pale in 1995 through your review and analysis of documents?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If you can look at the names of the people who were appointed to the staff, can you explain who these people are? If we look at the addressees, who or what is the police administration Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As of June 1995, the RS Ministry of Internal Affairs had its seat in Bijeljina in the north-eastern corner of Bosnia and Herzegovina, but it also maintained important offices at Pale, near Sarajevo. And indeed the documentation of the ministry during this period reflects that orders, instructions, decrees, et cetera, were issued both through the offices in Bijeljina and in Pale. In this case this document stems from Pale and is being issued by the deputy minister of MUP, Tomislav Kovac, who is establishing an operational staff of police forces in the zone in which a -- a state of war exists. The one that's referred to at the top, the staff of the command of police forces in MUP for -- located at Bijeljina, is basically the overall operational commanding unit for the field deployment and combat operations of MUP at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And I think you mentioned earlier that the special brigade commander was Goran Saric?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What was the role of the staff?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously when police forces are involved in day-to-day combat of an intense nature, as they were during this period, for example, at the Trnovo battle-field not far from Sarajevo, it is necessary to ensure that these forces are commanded operationally in a correct and efficient manner. And one of the purposes of having these police command staffs is to ensure that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender that document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2981, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I now want to look at a couple of documents regarding the relationship between the RS MUP and Serbian MUP units operating in the territory of the RS during June and July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter number 08208 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is a document dated the 24th of June, 1995, from the public security station Bratunac. It's addressed to the chief of Zvornik CSB. Who is that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As of June 1995, that was Dragomir Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you see Vasic's name on the document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it in handwriting at the top.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The document refers to MUP special -- MUP Serbia special task units (Frenki). What's this a reference to?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name or nickname Frenki is a reference to Franko Simatovic, who was a high-ranking employee of the State Security Service of the Republic of Serbia at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The Bratunac SJB commander is requesting information about whether the "deputy minister" has approved the stay of these ten Serbian MUP members. And you mentioned a moment ago that the deputy minister was Tomo Kovac. It then says: "... approved by President Karadzic and Tomo ..." Who is the Tomo referred to here?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given that the document already mentions the need for the deputy minister to approve the stay of these MUP Serbia units on the territory of the RS, I infer that this is a reference to Deputy Minister Tomislav Kovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And what, if anything, does this handwritten comment tell you about Karadzic's role in the deployment of Serbian MUP forces into the RS?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fact that not only the deputy minister of internal affairs but also the president of the RS, Dr. Karadzic, approved this shows to me that from the perspective of the MUP it was if not necessary at least highly desirable that Dr. Karadzic approve of this, and certainly in approving of it he would also had knowledge that such units were deployed on the territory of the RS.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender that document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But we don't know whose handwriting this is, Mr. -- Dr. Nielsen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if my memory were better than it was, I could probably -- many years ago I could have told you whose handwriting that is, but I can't off the top of my head. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, we are not opposed, but if there is other evidence that would be good if we received it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I tender that document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I was about -- wondering whether -- yes, we'll admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2982, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said taking into account your observation, Your Excellency, namely that we did not have information as to whose handwriting that was. So we are not opposed, taking into account your observation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we can take a look at another document, 65 ter number 01958.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is a document dated the 1st of July, 1995, from the special police brigade Trnovo from the special police brigade deputy commander Ljubisa Borovcanin dated -- and if we can look at the addressees. The document is sent to Tomo Kovac in his capacities as deputy minister and Pale police staff commander. Why would this report have been sent to Kovac in two different capacities?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kovac is at this point what one calls dual-hatted; that is, he is wearing several different functional titles within the RS MUP, but keeping in mind that the ministry was operationally co-located at both Pale and Bijeljina which were some distance apart, I see this, among other things, as an attempt to ensure that wherever he is he's going to receive this message and that both subordinates at Pale and Bijeljina will be duly informed of its contents.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And who is the Vogosca police forces staff?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not have detailed knowledge of that, but again any of these police force staffs in 1995 would have existed in areas in which intense operations were ongoing.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The document talks about two platoons from each of the Kajman, Plavi, Skorpija detachments (the MUP of Serbia) attacking a particular feature. We saw in the previous document that President Karadzic and Tomo Kovac personally approved the deployment of ten Serbian MUP members into Bratunac on the 24th of June, one week earlier. Does that tell you anything about who would have had to approve the deployment of the much bigger Kajman, Plavi, and Skorpija Serbian MUP units into the areas?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is both a leading and a misleading question. It has nothing to do with Bratunac, and we don't know whether that was approved in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I think you can reformulate the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, who in your view would have had to approve the deployment of this much bigger Kajman, Plavi, Skorpija Serbian MUP units into the RS?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two points. First, the language of the document in front of us is ambiguous as -- grammatically as to whether all three of these units are from MUP of Serbia or whether it is only the third of those units, the Skorpions, that belongs to MUP of Serbia. My second point would be that certainly the leadership of RS MUP would have known, as we can see here from this dispatch, that such units were located on the territory of the Serbian Republic. And given the fact that the deputy minister, Tomislav Kovac, was at this point in constant daily communication with the highest authorities of the republic, my assumption would be that they would also be aware of the presence of such units, particularly in light of the fact that a much smaller unit of mechanics that came from MUP of Serbia had apparently been the subject of notification to the Presidency. It would be curious if the deployment of an entire armed unit from MUP Serbia would not elicit similar notification.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. All these are extensive speculations. The assumption that I was informed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's subject of your cross-examination. Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So whose command are the Kajman, Plavi, and Skorpija operating under here?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know from other documents that these units were in the Trnovo battle-field area by around the 24th of June, I believe, 1995. And during that period they carried out combat operations together with the RS MUP units under the command of Goran Saric, who was the commander of the special police brigade at that point.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The document describes problems observing agreement with SRK command on joint action. Were these MUP units under the command of the SRK or were they working in co-ordination with them?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: During this period I believe the combat operations in the Trnovo area were being co-ordinated with the military forces that were in the area. I know from other documents that despite the type of agreement that this document refers to, the police was, once again, as in 1992, rather resentful of having in its own opinion to bear the brunt of the burden on the combat -- in the combat area.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And at what level does this co-ordination occur, at the staff level or lower down, at Borovcanin's level?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That certainly depends on what kind of co-ordination we're talking about. At the day-to-day/hour-by-hour co-ordination level, that would have been handled at the level of Borovcanin and people around him. But in terms of the decisions to deploy both police and military units, this could not have been taken without the involvement of the leadership of both the RS MUP and the Main Staff of the VRS, both of which were of course constituent parts of the armed forces of the RS, and hence ultimately subordinate to the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender that document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2983, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we can look at another document, 65 ter number 09274.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is a document dated the 6th of July, 1995, from Tomo Kovac, staff commander of the police forces Pale to the Sarajevo CJB and the Vogosca police forces staff. And you mentioned earlier that Tomo Kovac was also the deputy minister of MUP. And so can you explain why some documents are sent in his capacity as deputy minister and others in his capacity as staff commander?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I referred just a moment ago to his dual-hatted function. In cases during this period where Tomislav Kovac has to regulate matters that would normally be within the ambit of the minister of internal affairs, pursuant to the Law on Internal Affairs, he would send documents on that basis. In other cases - and this is one where it's essentially referring exclusively to combat operations, which again are within the ambit of a police forces staff - he logically sends such orders and informational reports, dispatches, et cetera, as -- in his capacity as the commander of the police staff at Pale which he had himself established.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In the first paragraph of the document it describes an offensive by the Herzegovina Corps and it's reported that 50 to 100 enemy soldiers died and 23 were captured. Would the capture of large groups of prisoners be something that the deputy minister of the RS MUP would have to be informed about?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly in combat situation reports, or sitreps, we see throughout this period that they include information on the number of enemy soldiers captured or killed, as well of course as information on the casualties incurred by the RS MUP, and that ultimately these reports would be communicated on to the deputy minister. Here it's actually an even more efficient reporting mechanism, that because in his capacity as direct commander of the police staff at Pale, he is himself reporting to other relevant units of the RS MUP on such activities and displaying knowledge of such.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Further down there's a reference in the document to special MUP forces of RS Serbia and the RSK. Can you tell us who these are?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From other dispatches that I have read from Trnovo, from this period, including the previous one, from Borovcanin, I take this to be a reference to the detachments including Kajman, Plavi, and Skorpija that were mentioned in earlier dispatches. They have a conglomeration of units present at Trnovo in early July 1995 which they refer to as the joint forces of RSK MUP, RS MUP, and MUP of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And down the bottom of the document Kovac reports that an offensive against Srebrenica began in the early hours of the 6th of July. Kovac then states that he would keep the recipients "posted on all the interesting events on this battle-field." Does this tell you anything about Kovac's level of notice, re: the events around Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read this as a clear intent that Kovac intends to stay abreast of the evolving security situation in the Srebrenica area and to report in the coming days on that situation, including the types of information that we would have seen in the sitrep.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can you tell from this document whether Kovac -- I'm sorry, I withdraw that. I want to look briefly at some of the sources of where Tomo Kovac and the MUP were receiving information from during this period. I don't want to get deeply into these, but I'm interested in who's providing who with information.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could have the first document 65 ter 18957, please. Your Honour, just while that's coming up, I tender the document 65 ter 09274.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P2984, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The document in front of us, 18957 is dated the 9th of July, 1995, and it's --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court who is the sender and who is the recipient?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The recipient is the RS Ministry of Internal Affairs cabinet at Pale as well as the staff of the command of police forces of the MUP at Bijeljina. And it's signed -- typed signed by Dragomir Vasic, but it has been signed for him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it Zvornik CSB or SJB?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may assist it is Zvornik CJB because at the beginning of 1994 all the CSBs were renamed as CJBs. This was because of a structural change that I perhaps should have mentioned earlier which is that in 1994 the State Security Services and -- or the State Security Service and the Public Security Service which had been earlier co-located in the CSB were separated out. So henceforth the Public Security Service would be in the CJB at the regional level and the State Security Service would be in the CRDB [Realtime transcript read in error "CRJB"] at the regional level.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2985, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The next document is 65 ter number 01943. And it's dated the 12th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Who is the sender and who is the recipient of this document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, please permit that I correct line 64 -- 16, it should be CRDB not CRJB. In this document in front of us now, the recipient is the deputy minister of internal affairs of the Republic of Serbia personally as well as the leader of -- or head, rather, of the Public Security Service who was, again, Milenko Karisik, again personally, and the dispatch is being sent by the head of the RDB, Dragan Kijac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And this document and the previous document are about the situation in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender that document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have a clarification. Is it Serbia or the Republika Srpska. In the transcript it is Serbia. It is written in the transcript of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: That's at -- on page 65, line 2. Dr. Nielsen, do you see --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is the deputy minister of internal affairs of the RS, not the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, this will be admitted as Exhibit P2986. And shall we take a break if it is convenient?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll have a break for an hour and resume at 1.30. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.30 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before we begin, I wanted to let the parties know that we are sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis for this session, with Judge Morrison being away due to his urgent personal matters. Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I continue in relation to Exhibit P2982 which was discussed at pages 56 to 58 of today's transcript, it was the document dated the 24th of June, 1995, from the public security station Bratunac to the public security centre Zvornik. And you inquired about the handwriting on the document. The MIF for the document for the Trial Chamber's benefit and Mr. Karadzic's says that the document was seized by the OTP from Mane Djuric at the Zvornik CSB. Of course, Mr. Nielsen has already -- Dr. Nielsen has already explained the difference between the CSB and the CJB at that point in time. So I note that for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That does not mean that it's -- it is his handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. It's simply -- I was just simply advising the Court and Mr. Karadzic as to where we got the document from, and it was seized on the 5th of June, 2002.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter number 01943 on the screen, please. Oh, I'm sorry, we've dealt with that document, that's Exhibit P2986. If I could have 65 ter number 04672, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is a document dated the 13th of July, 1995, and it's a dispatch from the SBP deputy commander Ljubisa Borovcanin to the Pale police staff. In this document Borovcanin describes how the MUP are involved in organising "the evacuation of the civilians from Srebrenica to Kladanj." He also describes that during the day, 13th of July, 1995, the MUP "captured or had surrendered to us, 15.000 [sic] Muslim soldiers. The number increases by the hour." Dr. Nielsen, in your opinion as the commander of the Pale police station to whom this report was sent, would Kovac have been made aware of the information contained in this report?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would note that this document was sent not to the commander of the Pale police station but to the command of the police staff at Pale who was, as we have seen in earlier documents today, Tomislav Kovac, so he is in fact one of the recipients of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2987, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could I have 65 ter number 01965 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is dated the 13th of July, 1995, and it's a dispatch from Tomo Kovac to the chief of the Zvornik CJB, passing on the information which Kovac -- sorry, who is Kovac receiving his information from, Dr. Nielsen?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular case, Kovac is forwarding information to the chief of CJB Zvornik, which he, Kovac, has obtained -- it's the text of a dispatch sent by the Drina Corps command of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is it a particular department within the corps?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It's the department for intelligence and security matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Exhibit P2988.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, I want you to now look at a log-book from the Republika Srpska state centre for encrypted communications, 65 ter number 02589. I want to take you in particular to entries from the 11th of July to the 16th of July. If we could look first at entries for the 11th of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And that is on the English page 4 and the B/C/S pages 2 to 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The entries for the 11th of July are numbered 2251, 2252, and 2253. If you could briefly explain to the Chamber those entries, please.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is 2250 -- excuse me, 2251, 2252, and 2253 are all referring to the same dispatch which is being received, it's a strictly confidential dispatch from the security organ of the Main Staff of the VRS and it's being distributed. The reason it's listed three times is that there were three different recipients, and for each recipient there's one entry in the log-book although it's the same dispatch and it arrives at the same time from the same sender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you know what is the state centre for encrypted communication?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I know that this was the central location in Pale at the time where security -- excuse me, where encrypted telegrams from various areas in the RS were being received and then distributed on to their recipients, many of whom were located at Pale.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It belonged to which organ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In this particular case I believe that these log-books were all confiscated from the RS MUP. I believe to the best of your knowledge and my recollection of these log-books that they were collected from the RS State Security Service and that the -- this communication centre was being operated by the RS State Security Service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could go to the 12th of July, this is page 6 of the English, page 3 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The entries that I would like you to focus on numbered 2265, 2266, and 2267.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again here this is a case of one dispatch, in this case it's from the following day, the 12th of July, 1995, again strictly confidential, again stemming from the VRS security organ and it's being distributed to three different recipients. It's -- one of which is the State Security Service of the RDB -- or RDB, one being the defence ministry, and one being the president.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The 13th of July which is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, but the first one, the number of the first one is different from the others, 2265. Is it translation problem? It says 12/45-840.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe in the B/C/S original it's because in the case of 2265 the handwriting is perhaps -- it's quite minuscule, and I believe that the person translating this document has erroneously put 840 instead of 860 because it's clearly reflected that 2265, 2266, and 2267 were all received at 0455 on the 12th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could go to the entries for the 13th of July, that's English page 10, B/C/S page 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The entries to focus on number 2298, 2299, and 22300 [sic].

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a similar occurrence. For the third day in a row at 0425 hours on the 13th of July, 1995, a dispatch is received from the security organ of the Main Staff of the VRS and is being sent, or rather, distributed by the communications centre to the president of the republic, the Ministry of Defence, and the State Security Service of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we can go to the 14th of July, this is at English page 12, B/C/S page 5, the entries to focus on numbered 2320, 2321, and 2322.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the exact same phenomenon recurring now on the 14th of July, 1995, at 0610 hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we can go to the entries on the 15th of July, that's English page 13 and 14 and B/C/S page 6. The entries to focus on are numbered 2334, 2335, and 2336.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is, again, the same pattern of communication recurring now on 15 July 1995 at 0715 hours. I just want to correct a statement I made a few moments ago because now that I look at the ERN number of the document I see that it is actually another log-book that looks very similar to another one I'm familiar with, that other one being from the State Security Service. In this case, I actually do not know exactly where it was located originally. So it may not be from the State Security Service.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we can go to entries for the 16th of July, this is English page 16, B/C/S page 7, the entries to focus on are numbered 2351, 2352, and 2353.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please all unnecessary microphones be switched off. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is again a similar pattern of communication now on the 16th of July, 1995, at 0525 hours. I would note just in passing that there are other instances in this log-book of communications that are also coming from the security organ of the VRS and that are also going to people located at Pale, including the president.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do the above-mentioned entries that we've just gone through from the 11th to the 16th of July show that every day during that period the VRS Main Staff security organ sent a report to the head of the RS MUP, Dragan Kijac, a representative from the Ministry of Defence, and also the president of the republic, Radovan Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is this consistent with communications functioning between the RDB and the other organs in the RS and the RSK and Serbia during this period?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Speaking purely based on this log-book, it's consistent with communications functioning between the RDB and other organs in the RS and between the security organs of the VRS and other organs in the RS. Based on the pages we've looked at here, I can't comment on the RSK and Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In your view, would information that was sent to Dragan Kijac and the president in these reports also have been made available to the deputy minister, Tomo Kovac?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the way in which the ministry functioned at the time, the minister or acting minister would have been privy to the information that was being collected by the State Security Service.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And have you ever seen one of these reports sent by the Main Staff security organ between the 11th and 16th of July, 1995, to Kijac and the president?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not. And in my capacity as an analyst who collected a large number of documents related to both the VRS and the RS MUP, I would point out that on recurring occasions in visiting archives in the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, we frequently found that the archive for the period covering July 1995 was missing.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender that document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, this will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2989, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Just on that point you say you haven't ever seen any of these reports, but are you aware of whether the Office of the Prosecutor possesses the reports?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have been informed by a military analyst of the Office of the Prosecutor that pursuant or after my departure from the OTP these dispatches that are listed in this log-book and which we were looking at here have not yet surfaced, they are not yet available.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I want to look now at other communication entries in the RS state security log-book of telegrams received.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And if 65 ter number 22831 could be brought up on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could look at entries for the 12th to the 18th of July, 1995, and that's in the B/C/S at pages 133 to 139 of the document. Dr. Nielsen, did you review the entries for the period 12 to 18 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. And with respect to this specific log-book, I would note that this one was definitely collected from the RS intelligence service and that's why -- I was involved in collecting it which is why a sticker with my name and signature appears on the cover.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The communications between the 12th and 18th of July, 1995, do those communications show that there was communications between the RDB and other organs in the RS, the RSK, and Serbia during this period?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And is this consistent with communications functioning?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I would now like you to look at another log-book from the RS state security log-book of telegrams sent, and that's --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry, if I could tender that document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What about the translation, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could either ask Dr. Nielsen to read out the headings and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Oh, I think we have the translation of the legend, but do you see the third column. Can you read all?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, do you see the third column?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the third column.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What's that heading?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The third column is "from whom."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I have that translation, but the content.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Between the 12th and 18th of July, is -- it's over a period of six pages. Could you tell the Court the names of the persons that the communications were received from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Which one is the first page? Is that the page we are looking at now?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that has the entries for the 12th -- at the beginning in the -- the column, the fifth column. You see it says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And then the next one 13.07.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I see. So if you are tendering six pages, why don't you ask this document to be translated only on that column?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Or would you like to --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, we'd --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- ask the witness to read out?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, we can actually have the -- for those six pages we will have the third column translated in full.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: But, Dr. Nielsen, can you advise the Chamber who of the -- which of the organs in the RS, RSK, and Serbia are these communications being received from?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for example, here we have communications being received from the Main Staff of the VRS, that's the third row on this page. We have a number of the CRDBs, the centres for state security that are sending information in. And on other pages we have references to other units of MUP in both the RS and MUP in Serbia. But again, I think the best thing rather than to go through all of these one by one would be to have a translation and then it can be seen on which basis I drew this conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll mark it for identification, pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI P2990, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter number 22833 which is the log-book from the Republika Srpska state -- it's the Republika Srpska state security log-book of telegrams sent.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And again, if we could look at entries from the 9th to the 16th of July, 1995, and that's on pages 182 to 188. Dr. Nielsen, if you can advise the Chamber of who the organs in the RS -- sorry, does that show -- have you -- I'll start again. Have you reviewed the entries between the 9th and the 16th of July, 1995, in this log-book?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Does it show that communications were being sent from -- between the RDB and other organs in the RS, RSK, and Serbia during this period?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This log-book is consistent with communications functioning among those institutions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And can you tell the Trial Chamber what organs within -- within the RS, RSK, and Serbia that these documents were being -- these communications were being sent from -- sent to?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in this case I believe, if I'm not mistaken, that this is a log-book of incoming dispatches. So it's a list of -- of the persons, or rather, institutions that are sending dispatches to the DB in the -- that is, the State Security Service in the RS and -- for example, the page that we have up on the screen now, we see a variety of, uh, originators of such communications. In some cases it's the Main Staff of the VRS. In some cases it's subordinate regional centres of the DB. In one case, the bottom entry on this page, it's the State Security Service in the MUP of the RSK. So there's a variety of -- and there's one from Serbia. So there's a variety of people who are communicating with the RDB during this period in July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can we just go to the first page of the document. The second page. And the third. And the following.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, the -- the log-book that we looked at a moment ago, exhibit -- which has been marked for identification, Exhibit P2920, I think you said that that was the log-book of telegrams received. This log-book that we're looking at now, is this a log-book of telegrams sent? Because I think you referred a moment ago to it being of telegrams received by the DB.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if we could go back to the page that I was commenting on before, it seemed to me that they had listed the communications in the column that says "from whom" and not "to whom."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: That's on page 182, please.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: So certainly in the B/C/S version just by looking at this page in isolation, the list with all the addresses is the column that says "from whom" not "to whom." To make any further inferences about the full nature of this particular log-book, I would have to review it in its entirety again. This is, again, a log-book that I have not reviewed in detail for a number of years, but certainly the fact that it says "from whom" tends -- if you list things in that column, it tends to be a list of communications that are being received, not sent.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, we will undertake to have the pages of the entries of the 9th to the 16th of July, 1995, translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI P2991, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The communications that we have seen, what does this tell you about the nature and the regularity of the communications between the organs of the RS, that is, the Presidency, the RS MUP, the Ministry of Defence, and the field during the period 10 to 16 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I infer from these log-books that despite the fact that we in many cases lack the dispatches that are referenced in these log-books, the log-books themselves lead to the conclusion or point towards the conclusion that communications were functioning regularly during this period because they list a very substantial number of communications among these institutions during this period of July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I now want to turn to look at an example of how the MUP implemented an order issued by the supreme commander, Karadzic, during this period.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter number 01964 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is dated the 10th of July, 1995, and if you could look at the addressees, please, and look at the sender. This is from Kovac in his capacity as staff commander. Are you aware of whether he personally signed this document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware that Tomislav Kovac has on many occasions, including in speaking to journalists, stated that he has never signed this order. He denies signing this order.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The document states that pursuant -- "on the order of -- of the supreme commander of the Republika Srpska armed forces," who is that a reference to?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a reference to the president of the republic, Dr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The document then describes the make-up of the MUP forces and appoints Ljubisa Borovcanin as its commander. It then orders Borovcanin to make contact with the Drina Corps Chief of Staff, General Krstic at that time. Can you tell the Trial Chamber what the relationship was between General Krstic and the MUP units described in this order?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pursuant to this order, the MUP units identified herein are to report by the mid -- middle of the day on 11 July 1995 to Bratunac. And once they get there, they are to be under the command or to -- rather, to report to the chief of the staff of the corps, General Krstic, where they were then supposed to receive further instructions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2992, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter number --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: 65 ter number --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- said that he did not sign it and that it would be more desirable to have an order that I had allegedly sent.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: We're getting there, Mr. Karadzic. If I could have 65 ter number 09214, please. This is a document dated the 10th of July, 1995, and it's a dispatch of the RS MUP deputy minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Again, did Kovac sign this document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is another example of the same document but not signed by Kovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know who it's signed by?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just want to make sure that I'm looking at the same document in B/C/S because I see that there's a discrepancy between the English document on the screen and the B/C/S document on the screen. The English translation says "signed for staff commander Tomislav Kovac," whereas the B/C/S version, as far as I can see, unless -- can the B/C/S version be scrolled down. Is there a second page? I don't think that this is the same document in English in B/C/S. That's the one, yes. That looks more familiar. In this case, it's signed for Kovac by an R. Nikolic, and I take that to be a reference to the Nikolic who is identified in the document we saw earlier today establishing the police staff at Pale. He was a member of that staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is it R. Nikolic or D. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may be permitted to look back at the staff establishment document. I take it to be R. Nikolic, as in Radomir Nikolic, who is number 6 on the -- original -- uh, form. But again, I would say that's with a bit of, uh, uncertainty, mainly for the reason that, uh -- the handwriting is not quite distinct. But I make it out to be an R, and that would have been the only R. Nikolic on the staff of the police at Pale is Radomir Nikolic who is identified in 65 ter 23116 -- or excuse me, 23166.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But it's certainly not signed by Kovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- I seek to tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Probably you need to remove the first page of the B/C/S, which is not translated.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. This will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2993, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And I take it, Dr. Nielsen, that this is a different version of the previous document we just saw, Exhibit P2992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. There are a great many copies of that document that were found in various archives of the RS MUP.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Just getting back to the, um, Nikolic -- do you know a person called Dragomir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've heard of that person.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Who is that person?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe, as far as I know, that that was a person who at the time of the events in Srebrenica in July 1995 was serving in the VRS as an officer. I don't at the moment recall his position, his exact function.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I want to look now at another example of a presidential order being implemented.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter number 01885 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is a document dated the 11th of July, 1995, entitled: "Republika Srpska Presidential Directive." And it's an order on the establishment of an office of a public security station in Serbian Srebrenica. What is the significance of this document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once Srebrenica came under Serbian control after the 11th of July of 1995, there were steps taken by the authorities of the RS to establish all of the types of organs that one would have functioning at the municipal level, including, as we see here, a paragraph -- a -- a public security station, in this case for what they have now termed Serbian Srebrenica. And it's stated that this station will function pursuant to the Law on Internal Affairs and will also establish close co-operation with Miroslav Deronjic, the highest civilian official in Srebrenica at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender that document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2994.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter number 01898 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is a document dated the 12th of July, 1995. What is this document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document of the RS Ministry of Internal Affairs from the office of the minister that is forwarding verbatim an order of the president of the republic to the Zvornik public security centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And when you say an order of the president of the republic, is that the order that we saw in the previous document, P2994?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender that document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2995, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And again, just to remind us, who was the chief of the Zvornik public security centre?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dragomir Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter number 01929 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is a document also dated the 12th of July, 1995. What does this report show?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This -- well, the essence certainly of the beginning of this report from Dragomir Vasic, the chief of CJB Zvornik is to report back to the Ministry of Internal Affairs and to the minister -- office of the minister that he is acting in accordance with the order that we just saw, which originally stemmed from the president.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And what sort of co-ordination does it show?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- in addition to showing that Vasic is carrying out the orders of the president as transmitted through the minister or the office of the minister, this also shows that the police is closely co-ordinating with the top generals of the VRS. Here we have General Mladic and General Krstic on the second point of the dispatch. And it shows an awareness of the concentration of a large number of Muslims at Potocari and an awareness that others are fleeing. It also discusses meetings with UNPROFOR, the International Red Cross, and other relevant operations that are taking place in Srebrenica at that time. And it states finally that Vasic will keep the minister promptly informed of all further facts and developments.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And is there also co-ordination with Deronjic?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As stated in paragraph 1 of the dispatch, he is implementing the president's order transmitted through the minister to contact the civilian commissioner in Bratunac, Miroslav Deronjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And what's the significance of the fact that it describes how they're going to evacuate the civilian population and how the joint police forces are advancing?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see these as pertinent and relevant amounts of information that are being provided by Dragomir Vasic to his superiors. I mean, he's showing that communications are functioning at that time in both directions, and as such that also means that the chain of command is functioning in both directions. He's showing that he's implementing an order that he's received that ultimately stems from the president of the republic. On the other hand, he's also showing that he's engaging in various co-ordination activities and that he is aware of the need to keep his superiors informed of all important events.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender that document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2996, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: May we now look at another document, 65 ter number 21253.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is a very urgent dispatch dated the 12th of July, 1995. What is the significance of this document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, what we see here is that the Ministry of Internal Affairs is distributing verbatim an order of the president of the republic to subordinate organs of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the RS. In this particular order it again pertains to events that are relevant to security, in this case humanitarian convoys passing through, and talks about the need for co-ordination among the organs of the state in a view to permitting but also controlling the passage of such convoys through the territory of the RS.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I think if we can go to page 2 of the English, this is referred to in paragraph 8; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's also referred to in paragraph 8. It's also referred to already in paragraph 1, that this is focusing on humanitarian convoys.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And are there legal consequences or sanctions?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the final paragraph of the transmitted order from the president of the republic, it's stated that this is a matter to be taken extremely seriously and that therefore anyone who hinders or neglects to implement this order will face swift legal sanctions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Does this show co-operation between the organs?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And it shows within a day of the president issuing the order it was passed on to the subordinate organs of the RS MUP verbatim?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2997, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And the second-to-last document I wish you to look at is 65 ter number 13605. This is dated the 15th of July, 1995. Who is this communication between?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is from the office of the minister of the internal affairs in the RS to the Zvornik CJB. It's a -- it's the text of a proclamation or a -- rather, a decision on the proclamation of a state of war in Srebrenica, Skelani municipality, originally written by the president of the republic on the previous day.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender that document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2998, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And what's the difference between this dispatch that we see here and the previous one, Exhibit P2997?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well my --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In relation to reporting. Do we see any commentary, for example, from the RS MUP in this document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there is -- at this stage there's no comment. It's just saying that we are forwarding to you a decision. And then you have the text of the decision, and then you have the typed signature of the deputy minister, Tomislav Kovac. There's no editorial comment or annotation being offered in this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I now wish to show you a document which is the agenda of Mr. Karadzic and that's Exhibit P02242. This is his agenda for the 2nd of January to the 25th of December, 1995, but I want to look at entries between the 10th and the 14th of July, 1995, that's on the English page 77 to 80 and in the B/C/S pages 89 to 91. Looking first at the entry for 10th of July, can you point out for the Trial Chamber the MUP names that are contained within this agenda?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Before doing so let me just amend the last sentence of my previous response which was there's no editorial comment or annotation being offered in this document. In -- on the 10th of July in this agenda we see that Dr. Karadzic's meeting with Dragan Kijac and Milenko Karisik who are respectively the heads of state and public security at the time in RS MUP, he meets with them from 1700 to 1720 hours. We then have -- two lines below that we have Zika Rakic, this is the minister, in fact, of internal affairs at the time from 1935 to 2005 hours. Those are the people that I immediately recognise from RS MUP with which he meets on the 10th of July. If we could go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Looking at the 11th of July.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the 11th of July -- well, the first thing I note is that he meets at -- from 1910 to 1920 hours for ten brief minutes he meets with Stojan Zupljanin, who is admittedly no longer in the MUP at that point but was of course the former head of the CSB in Banja Luka and was at the time of July 1995 a security advisor to Dr. Karadzic, to the president. So that's relevant from the point of view of the police. And his last meeting on the 11th of July is with Milenko Karisik, the chief of the Public Security Service of RS MUP from 2230 to 2245 hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we can go to the 13th of July, which is the following -- and over on to the following page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right. Here we have from 1550 to 1610 hours we have a meeting with Tomo Kovac, who was the deputy minister of internal affairs and, as I previously stated, was de facto operating as the minister of internal affairs in many respects at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we can go to the entry for the 14th of July.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not seeing anyone here from RS MUP immediately --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we can go --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- that I recognise.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- to the following page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I see Tomo Kovac listed near the bottom in a meeting where the prime minister -- or as he's referred to here President Krajisnik also attended, starting at 1615 and most likely going on until 1745 hours, given that the following meeting started at 1755.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you --

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I also -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Where do we have the --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: At the top of the English on the 14th of July, do you see Tomo Kovac in the agenda for 2245 to 2310 hours?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think I overlooked that one.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And so the -- the one that you were just referring to at the bottom of the page, is that on the 14th?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one I just referred to is on the 15th --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: On the 15th, I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- from 1415 to probably 1745, and that's cut off.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, and that's the one that's on page 80 of the English translation. If we could go over the following page. No, I'm sorry, now I'm confusing you --

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, now I see it at the bottom of the English page in front of me here, third-to-last line.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes. And that's on the 15th of July? Thank you, doctor --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, just a matter in relation to Exhibit P2993 which was 65 ter number 23116 [sic]. That was the document that you said that we should remove the first page of the B/C/S because we didn't have a translation. In fact, both pages of the B/C/S need to remain in the exhibit because the first page of the exhibit is translated. It's the typed signed version, and the other page which has been admitted is the original, signed version. So it's a signed version and a typed document which are the same, the content is the same, and we have the English translation for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we have the confirmation from the witness? I remember, Witness, that that document was not identical to the translated one. Shall we upload it --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could call it up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Exhibit P2993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Only the B/C/S. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was told that they are so quick as to remove the page already.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I have the document here, we could put it on e-court -- sorry, ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just for your information, the 65 ter number of this is 9214. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it is. I'm sorry, I misspoke when I said it was 23166. The reference to 23166 was the reference that Dr. Nielsen made in relation to -- when he spoke about Dragomir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I will leave it in the assessment of the witness. Doctor, could you compare the pages and -- two pages and then whether you can tell us the contents of them are identical, as indicated by Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
