utterances.text: I agree that these are two versions of the same order. In one which is merely typed, the other which is typed and signed for Tomislav Kovac, by someone whose last name was Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Then we'll reinstate the first page.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And I'm advised that the page is back in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, that completes my examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honours, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karadzic, are you ready to start?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Excellency, I am ready. But I was wondering whether perhaps it would be better if I started from the beginning on Tuesday and not stop after 20 minutes. Of course it is up to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't you put some introductory questions and then we'll adjourn for this week.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Doctor.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I should like to ask you whether you had been in Yugoslavia prior to these wars?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The first time I visited the territory of what used to be Yugoslavia was in 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And is anyone -- does anyone from -- does any member of your family hail from Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm married to someone from the former Yugoslavia if that's included in your definition of family, but my parents and my -- the rest of my family are all from Denmark.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where exactly your wife comes from?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly, she's from Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It doesn't matter. The witness has answered the question, Your Honour, but I was wondering as to the relevance of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I was just interested how come that Dr. Nielsen wanted to learn Serbo-Croat, and I wanted to know whether -- with whom he had close contacts and whether his contacts could have in any way influenced his options.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: My wife has a great influence in me. Can the same be said in respect of you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's proceed, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, did you know, were you familiar with the pre-war political system, what was referred to as self-managing socialism?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was part of my training as a historian, to familiarise myself with that topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that that had been a mono-party system and basically a profoundly undemocratic system?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree that what existed in socialist Yugoslavia was a mono-party system that operated according to the party state principle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would it be fair to say that in that system as well there existed in the republics that had a number of constituent peoples, such as Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina, were there -- there existed the obligation on proportionate or parity representation of those constituent nations as well as of the others, the so-called national minorities, in the governments in the rule of the respective countries -- or republics, rather?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And that that was also the case in respect of the distribution of executive positions in socially owned enterprises, in public enterprises, namely, that account was always taken of that principle, and when Bosnia and Herzegovina is concerned and probably also pre-war Croatia, that was something which was also reflected in their constitutions, i.e., legislation generally?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree with me that that one and only party which was in power decided what members of the party, Serbs, Croats, and Muslims, would represent their national communities in the bodies of government and in all places where proper ethnic representation had to be promoted. Do we agree that that party, the only existing party and the party in power - as there was no opposition - actually designated what Croat, what Serb, what Muslim would hold a specific office or position?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in that period numerous intellectuals from all the three national communities, ethnic communities, including yours truly and my closest associates, had been dissidents opposing that system for many decades?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that there were many dissidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that before the 1990 elections, the state administration, the state services, the bureaucracy generally, the state apparatus as a whole had not been divested of its party or political characters, but on the contrary, membership of the party greatly determined one's position in the state apparatus?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you familiar of the -- with the concept of negative selection which designated poor selections or elections within the state apparatus or to state offices because the one who could better ingratiate himself with the party in power was the one who was appointed to a specific office?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do we agree that it was inconceivable for any executive position, for instance, in the police, to leave aside the other services, for appointments to be made to such positions were -- of people who were not members of the League of Communists?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that's why they called it a party state.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So anyone who was not a member of the party could not be elected or appointed -- appointed to a position, to an executive or a leadership position; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that if they wanted to replace someone, first of all the municipal party committee or his basic chapter of the League of Communists would make such a decision; and then if such a decision was brought at that level, the person in question would also be dismissed at other levels?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is something that I'm familiar with.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you agree with me that at the 1990 elections there was a replacement of not only the regime but also of the system, and that the system of self-managing socialism and the mono-party autocracy, not to say dictatorship, was actually replaced thanks to the electoral will of the citizens and that replacing it was the multi-party system which was then introduced?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree with you partially. I agree that the mono-party state system was replaced. It was, subsequent events showed, replaced by three parties who in large measure all tried to create their own party state systems using the types of political rules that they'd been familiar with from the previous system.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That was in fact my next question, but you have pre-empted me. I should like to ask you this: Do you remember that the Serbian Democratic Party was the last one to be founded of the ethnically determined parties and that I personally actually spoke against that ethno-democracy?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that actual statement. I'm not disagreeing with you that that statement was made, but I do recall certainly the Serbian Democratic Party was the last one of the three ethnically determined parties founded, and I recall that Alija Izetbegovic was among the guests at the establishment of that party.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That is correct. Thank you. And do you remember that after the 1990 elections I proposed that we should not elect a party-based government but a government of experts and that the two other parties in our coalition did not accept that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that the constitution of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina was amended in the summer of 1990 towards the end of July, just a few months prior to the elections?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not an expert on constitutional arrangements, but I believe that you are correct in making that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm not asking you in the legal sense, but historically speaking was that a fact, did it happen that way?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only reiterate my previous answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the assumption that you believe me, is it customary in democratic systems for a constitution to be amended in a year of elections and not to say three months, let alone three months, prior to elections?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not an expert on constitutional law and election systems, but I would tend to agree with you that that is unusual.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In that case probably you cannot give me an answer to this, that we ask that instead of the chamber of associated labour, in addition to the chamber of citizens and the chamber of municipalities, there should be introduced in the Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina a chamber of nations which would see that there would be no engineering of a majority and out-voting in that sense, so as to prevent any political upheavals and convulsions on that account?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right, I cannot give you an answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it your view that it would have been good if you knew that, that that would have cast a certain light on your perception of some other facts?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think it's part of the overall political background which I try -- certainly the general political background of the period from November 1990 until April 1992 that I have as the background for my report. But basically I left political matters over to the expertise of other experts and focused mainly on the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you perhaps happen to learn that our proposal was not accepted, but they comforted us by introducing a national equality council which would not be a permanent chamber of citizens but would be an ad hoc chamber of citizens. When 20 MPs demanded that something be discussed by the council, it could not be done until the council accepted such a decision. Were you aware of such a council which was, in fact, as a substitute for what we were actually asking for?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the first part of the -- the introductory part, perhaps, the very first paragraph of the introduction you say that the control of political forces in Bosnia and Herzegovina was a component and key element in the attempts of the Bosnian Serb leadership to achieve their primary goals. And in paragraph 2 you state: "The development of this view has to be understood in the overall context of Bosnian Serb ideology in 991 to 992." And then you go on to say, namely: "The SDS consistently expressed dissatisfaction with the steps taken by Bosnian Muslim and Bosnian Croat politician on the BH's path to independence." I should like to ask you this: Do you agree our primary goals, the primary objectives of the Serbian Democratic Party and our ideology are in fact contained in our programme, in our founding programme, as well as in our pre-election programme which actually won us the votes of almost all Serbs there?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you familiar with the programme of the Serbian Democratic Party established and accepted in 1990 at establishment and confirmed in 1991 on the 12th of July, on St. Peter's day?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have in the past read that programme.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. That's probably understood in B/C/S. Could you put a pause between the question and the answer. So your previous answer was not noted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. My previous answer was: Yes, I have read that programme.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, whenever it is convenient, we will adjourn. And there's one matter the Chamber wants to clarify.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we can adjourn now as far as I'm concerned. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, not to pre-empt the Chamber, I will just need two minutes as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please go ahead, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. With respect to 65 ter 30115, that was the intercept that was raised yesterday to which Mr. Robinson objected because that intercept had not been put to Mr. Mandic, which provoked a discussion about whether the issue had been raised before. I know the Court indicated that it would leave -- leave that matter for the moment and come back to it another time, but Mr. Robinson's e-mail to the Chamber has sort of forced my hand at this moment. So I wanted to respond to the Court's inquiry about when that was previously raised and what the nature of it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure about Mr. Robinson's e-mail to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, to the Legal Officer in any event -- well, in any event, we'll leave that for now. I'll respond, if I may then, to the Court's inquiry about where that discussion took place, and it was on two days, the 25th of February, 2011, and then the 28th of February, 2011. So first it came up and then the argument -- or the discussion about it continued, but the relevant point to which I want to draw the Court's attention was on the 28th of February at pages -- the argument then or the submission by the Prosecution is made at 12480 through 12482. I won't go into the details and I'm prepared to supplement those if necessary, but I don't think that's the case. But what happened was basically there were 14 intercepts, some included by Mr. Mandic. The argument was made by the Defence that we heard yesterday, and the Court's ruling was that it would admit intercepts that had been sufficiently contextualised by the witness but would not at this -- at that time admit intercepts for which there was only voice recognition provided. And the Court noted explicitly that, of course, the Prosecution would be able to use that evidence of voice recognition later to authenticate the intercepts when they were tendered again. And there was another reference in the same general portion to the fact that the intercepts could -- could be tendered again and that the anticipation was they would be tendered again. So I would say it's a very clear rejection of the argument that the Mandic-related intercepts could not be tendered because they had not been put to Mr. Mandic. I would further note that that understanding of the Court's decision was apparently shared by the Defence because the Defence itself introduced an intercept of Mr. Mandic on 21 March 2011, if not on other occasions, but I found at least one. And that was D -- now MFI D1239. So I think everyone shares the understanding that the submission of the intercept is not precluded, provided that it otherwise fits within the guide-lines - in this case it clearly does - it was contextualised by a witness and it should be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger. This may only concern you, Mr. Robinson, and probably the Victims and Witnesses Section of the Tribunal. On 5th of July, 2011, upon the accused's request, the Chamber issued a subpoena ordering General Sead Delic to submit to an interview with the accused's legal advisor. At this stage the Chamber wishes to clarify that the language of the subpoena in no way implies that the Victims and Witness Section of the Tribunal should be responsible for organising the interview and for covering the costs incurred therein. Rather, the Chamber reminds the accused that it is for him to make all the necessary arrangements for these interviews to be conducted. In addition, the Chamber reminds the accused that he has resources available to him to cover costs incurred during the investigative stage and that it is for him to file the appropriate requests. I hope that clarifies the matter. We'll have a long weekend and we'll resume on Tuesday at 9.00. And, Dr. Nielsen, I didn't tell you yesterday but you are familiar with the rule that you are not supposed to discuss with anybody about your testimony here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll rise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 12th day of July, 2011, at 9.00 a.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.59 p.m.,
